paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Bildad and Job both talk about how BIG God is, but they land in two very different places. Bildad looks at God's greatness and says man is "but a maggot" and "but a worm!" (Job 25:6). Job looks at the same God and says the dead tremble, the earth hangs on nothing, and the foundations of heaven quake (Job 26:5, 7, 11).

Here's the difference I see. Bildad uses God's greatness to shrink a person down until there's nothing left. Job uses it to stand in awe, and he starts by asking Bildad, "And whose spirit spoke through you?" (Job 26:4). I think that's worth a pause, because you can say true things about God and still miss how He is treating the one who's hurting. Big words about God are not the same as good help for a friend, and I've given plenty of both myself.

And then Job says the part that stops me every time: all of this is "but the fringes of His ways," and "how faint is the whisper we hear of Him!" (Job 26:14). Hanging the earth on nothing is the WHISPER, baker. So when life leaves you with questions you can't answer, you don't have to pretend you've figured God out. You can stand in awe of Him and keep listening, and I'm telling you, this story isn't over.
